subject: Sunrise Hardware onboarding — PO issuance, spend cap, and line item mapping

From: Ethan Shaw <ethan@sunrisehardware.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@sunrisehardware.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sunrise Hardware onboarding — PO issuance and spend cap questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood's onboarding checklist yesterday. We attached our completed vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and a first-pass invoice spreadsheet (sunrise_po_request.xlsx). Two quick items before we finalize:

1) PO issuance: Our AP team needs a PO number that we can reference on the initial invoice (there's one invoice ready once you confirm the PO). Do you issue a provisional PO while finance completes coding, or should we wait for the final PO?

2) Spend cap and line items: We requested an elevated spend cap of $75,000 for Q1 — is that something you can set immediately for an initial deployment? Also, the spreadsheet includes three hardware SKUs that may be split across two internal line codes on our side. Can you confirm how Redwood prefers line items to be mapped (purchase_ref vs sku)?

Appreciate a short timeline so our AP/Distro team can schedule shipment.

Thanks,
Ethan Shaw
Procurement Manager
Sunrise Hardware

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_form.pdf (pdf), sunrise_po_request.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks Ethan — summarized below and next steps.

On Wed, 10 Mar 2027 at 9:12 AM Ethan Shaw <ethan@sunrisehardware.com> wrote:
> Hi Olga,
> 
> Thanks again for walking us through Redwood's onboarding checklist yesterday. We attached our completed vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and a first-pass invoice spreadsheet (sunrise_po_request.xlsx). Two quick items before we finalize:
> 
> 1) PO issuance: Our AP team needs a PO number that we can reference on the initial invoice (there's one invoice ready once you confirm the PO). Do you issue a provisional PO while finance completes coding, or should we wait for the final PO?
> 
> 2) Spend cap and line items: We requested an elevated spend cap of $75,000 for Q1 — is that something you can set immediately for an initial deployment? Also, the spreadsheet includes three hardware SKUs that may be split across two internal line codes on our side. Can you confirm how Redwood prefers line items to be mapped (purchase_ref vs sku)?

Short answers: we can issue a provisional PO (PROV-####) immediately so your AP team can proceed; Finance will replace it with a final PO after ledger coding (usually 1–3 business days). Default provisional spend cap is $50,000; we can raise to $75,000 if you provide the justification on page 2 of the onboarding form (looks like you included the note — thanks).

Line item guidance: please send the mapping matrix as a single worksheet with three columns: your_sku, your_line_code, invoice_description. Redwood's procurement system maps vendor SKU -> purchase_ref when we ingest invoices; for split lines we prefer that each invoice line reference the purchase_ref we provide. To avoid duplication, please flag any bundle rows and mark them in the spreadsheet.

Next steps (action owners):
- Ben (cc) will open the procurement ticket and assign a provisional PO.
- Sunrise: update sunrise_po_request.xlsx with the three-column mapping (your_sku / your_line_code / invoice_description) and resend.
- Marissa (cc): will confirm whether Finance can expedite coding once provisional PO is assigned.

I'll attach a short onboarding_checklist.pdf that shows what Finance needs. Expect a provisional PO within the hour after Ben opens the ticket.

Olga Petrov
Procurement Lead | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachment: onboarding_checklist.pdf (pdf)
